docs.title: Enterprise AI Platform
docs.text:
A production-grade AI control plane for enterprise developer tooling, governance, and secure provider orchestration.

::: tip Project Vision The Enterprise AI Platform enables organizations to centrally manage AI interactions, enforce policy, preserve tenant isolation, and operationalize provider routing across developer tools. :::

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The platform uses a Clean Architecture service model with bounded-context services for identity, policy, routing, provider adapters, knowledge, prompt intelligence, and observability.

  • Service-oriented architecture with independently deployable bounded contexts
  • API/Host layer for transport, authentication, OpenAPI, and health checks
  • Infrastructure layer for persistence, provider integrations, and caching
  • Application layer for use cases, validation, and orchestration
  • Domain layer for business rules, aggregates, and tenant-aware invariants

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text:
• Platform: .NET 9, ASP.NET Core
  • Data: PostgreSQL, Redis
  • Observability: OpenTelemetry, structured logging
  • API docs: OpenAPI + Scalar + MkDocs Material
  • Testing: xUnit, integration/contract tests
  • Client: VS Code extension and developer tooling integrations

docs.text:
• src/ — service source code, adapters, and host projects
  • clients/ — VS Code extension and client integrations
  • tests/ — unit, integration, and architecture tests
  • docs/ — documentation portal and governance artifacts
  • outputs/ — generated architecture reports and diagrams

docs.text:

docs.title: Reporting and Contribution
docs.text:

docs.title: ADRs
docs.text: This directory stores Architectural Decision Records for major platform decisions.

docs.title: ADR template
docs.text: • ADR Template

docs.title: Decision records
docs.text:
• ADR-0001 Clean Architecture
  • ADR-0002 .NET 9
  • ADR-0003 PostgreSQL
  • ADR-0004 Redis
  • ADR-0005 Docker

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: We need a structure that keeps domain logic independent from transport, persistence, and provider integrations.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use Clean Architecture with inward dependencies and bounded-context service slices.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Core rules stay testable
  • Infrastructure can change without rewriting business logic
  • Each service owns its own composition root

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: .NET 9 provides the current application platform baseline for the repository.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Target .NET 9 across the solution.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Shared language and library baseline
  • Native OpenAPI support is available
  • Platform services stay aligned with current runtime features

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The platform requires a relational store with strong ecosystem support and reliable transactional behavior.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use PostgreSQL for persistence-backed service slices.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Natural fit for EF Core
  • Good support for JSON, indexing, and extensions
  • Operational model is familiar for cloud deployments

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Caching, rate limiting, and distributed coordination need a low-latency shared store.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use Redis for cache and distributed state where needed.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Faster repeated reads
  • Shared resilience and quota state
  • Extra operational dependency to manage

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The platform needs a consistent, portable runtime environment for development, CI, and deployment.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use Docker to containerize services and support consistent build, test, and deployment workflows.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Services become reproducible across environments
  • Local development and CI deployments can share container images
  • The platform aligns with cloud-native deployment patterns

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The platform needs a modern, interactive API documentation experience over native OpenAPI output.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Use Scalar as the API documentation UI on top of ASP.NET Core native OpenAPI.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Better developer experience than static docs alone
  • No separate Swagger UI stack is needed
  • OpenAPI stays generated from the application itself

docs.title: API Guidelines
docs.text:
• Use native ASP.NET Core OpenAPI generation.
  • Version APIs from day one.
  • Group endpoints by module using route groups and tags.
  • Keep request and response DTOs explicit and stable.
  • Require authentication for tenant-scoped operations.
  • Prefer problem details for failures.
  • Document all public endpoints with XML comments.

docs.title: Documentation Rules
docs.text:
• OpenAPI document is generated from the running application.
  • Scalar is the interactive API UI.
  • JWT Bearer security must appear in the schema.
  • Health endpoints remain available for platform probes.

docs.title: API Overview
docs.text: This page describes the API standards for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Provide a consistent experience for API consumers.
  • Define the platform's API behavior without implementing endpoints.
  • Support versioned, secure, and discoverable APIs.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• Use explicit request and response models.
  • Document all public endpoints with OpenAPI.
  • Keep APIs stable and versioned.
  • Enforce tenant isolation and authorization.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: This page defines API authentication standards for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Secure API access for tenant and developer clients.
  • Standardize authentication mechanisms for all services.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Use JWT Bearer tokens for protected APIs.
  • Support API key-based access for tooling and internal clients where needed.
  • Document authentication requirements in the OpenAPI schema.
  • Reject anonymous requests for tenant-scoped operations.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: This page defines API error handling standards for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Provide consistent error responses for clients.
  • Make API failures observable and actionable.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Use RFC 7807 Problem Details for API errors.
  • Include type, title, status, and detail fields.
  • Provide instance or traceId when available.
  • Maintain consistent status codes for common failure categories.

docs.title: Response Standards
docs.text: This page defines response standards for the Enterprise AI Platform APIs.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Ensure API responses are consistent and predictable.
  • Support client integration and stability.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Use explicit DTOs for request and response bodies.
  • Avoid returning domain entities directly.
  • Include metadata only when necessary.
  • Keep responses compact and clear.

docs.title: Response Design
docs.text:
• Use JSON as the default response format.
  • Include pagination metadata for list endpoints.
  • Use consistent naming for fields and objects.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: This page defines API versioning standards for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Ensure backward compatibility for external clients.
  • Support gradual API evolution.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Use versioned routes under /api/v1/ for production APIs.
  • Keep version information in the URL path, not in headers.
  • Introduce v2, v3, etc. only when breaking changes are required.
  • Document supported versions in OpenAPI.

docs.title: ADR Standards
docs.text: This page defines standards for Architectural Decision Records (ADRs).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Capture architecture decisions, context, and consequences.
  • Maintain a searchable decision history.
  • Align decisions with platform and enterprise requirements.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
• Use the ADR template in ../adr/adr-template.md.
  • Keep ADRs short and structured.
  • Include context, decision, alternatives, and consequences.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text:
• Use sequential ADR IDs: ADR-0001, ADR-0002, etc.
  • Use a descriptive title after the identifier.
  • Keep file names consistent with the ADR title.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
• Create an ADR for decisions that affect architecture, security, or platform behavior.
  • Review ADRs in PRs and keep them current.
  • Reference ADRs from related documentation and release notes.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: Enterprise AI Platform follows Clean Architecture and bounded-context service slices. Each service owns its domain model, application use cases, infrastructure adapters, and API/host composition root.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text:
• Domain: aggregates, entities, value objects, and domain rules
  • Application: use cases, commands, queries, orchestration, and contracts
  • Infrastructure: persistence, external integrations, caching, queues, telemetry
  • API/Host: transport, authentication, OpenAPI, health checks, and routing

docs.title: Platform Principles
docs.text:
• Services are independently deployable
  • External AI providers are isolated behind adapter abstractions
  • Shared building blocks contain only cross-cutting primitives
  • APIs expose versioned contracts and documented endpoints

docs.title: Coding Standards
docs.text:
• Target .NET 9
  • Use nullable reference types
  • Prefer immutable records for contracts
  • Keep public APIs documented
  • Favor asynchronous APIs for I/O
  • Keep domain logic inside the domain layer
  • Use clear names over clever abstractions

docs.title: Documentation Style Guide
docs.text: This page defines the documentation style guide for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Maintain consistent tone and presentation across the docs portal.
  • Reduce friction for new contributors writing documentation.
  • Ensure documentation is clear, concise, and enterprise-ready.

docs.title: Tone and Voice
docs.text:
• Use professional, neutral language.
  • Prefer direct and active voice.
  • Avoid jargon without context.
  • Keep paragraphs short and scannable.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
• Use headings to outline sections clearly.
  • Use paragraphs, lists, and callouts for readability.
  • Keep content focused on one concept per section.

docs.title: Formatting
docs.text:
• Use sentence case for headings.
  • Use code formatting for commands, file names, and paths.
  • Keep list items short and parallel.
  • Use admonitions for important notes, warnings, and tips.

docs.title: Review
docs.text:
• Update documentation with every significant code or design change.
  • Review docs as part of pull request quality checks.

docs.title: Folder Structure Standards
docs.text: This page defines folder structure standards for the documentation portal and repository.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Ensure documentation is organized and discoverable.
  • Keep the repository layout intuitive for contributors.
  • Maintain clear separation between documentation categories.

docs.title: Docs Folder Structure
docs.text:
• Use top-level folders for major categories such as getting-started, architecture, api, deployment, security, observability, testing, operations, troubleshooting, adr, and diagrams.
  • Use assets for supporting images and files.
  • Use index.md as the landing page for each category.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text:
• Use lowercase names and hyphens for directory names.
  • Keep folder names brief and descriptive.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
• Add new categories only when there is a clear need.
  • Keep related docs grouped within the same folder.
  • Review the folder structure when adding major new content areas.

docs.title: Markdown Standards
docs.text: This page defines Markdown standards for the Enterprise AI Platform documentation.

docs.title: General Rules
docs.text:
• Use UTF-8 encoding.
  • Keep line lengths readable (80-120 characters where practical).
  • Use headings to organize content hierarchically.
  • Prefer fenced code blocks for code examples.

docs.title: Headings
docs.text:
• Use # for top-level sections.
  • Use incremental heading levels without skipping levels.
  • Use sentence case for heading text.

docs.title: Code Blocks
docs.text:
• Use triple backticks for code blocks.
  • Specify the language when possible.
  • Keep examples minimal and relevant.

docs.title: Lists
docs.text:
• Use hyphens for bullet lists.
  • Keep list items concise.
  • Use proper punctuation consistently.

docs.title: Links and References
docs.text:
• Use relative links for repository docs.
  • Use absolute URLs for external references.
  • Keep link text descriptive and actionable.

docs.title: Mermaid Standards
docs.text: This page defines Mermaid standards for the Enterprise AI Platform documentation.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Keep diagrams consistent and maintainable.
  • Use Mermaid for architecture and workflow visuals.
  • Keep diagrams simple and easy to update.

docs.title: General Rules
docs.text:
• Use graph, flowchart, sequenceDiagram, or classDiagram as appropriate.
  • Keep each diagram focused on a single concept.
  • Use descriptive node labels and avoid overloaded visuals.
  • Use comments sparingly for readability.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
• Wrap Mermaid code in fenced blocks with mermaid.
  • Use consistent spacing and indentation.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Client] --> B[API]
    B --> C[Service]
```

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Prefer flowcharts for architecture diagrams.
  • Use sequence diagrams for request and authentication flows.
  • Use labels to clarify participant roles.
  • Keep complex diagrams split into smaller diagrams.

docs.title: Naming Conventions
docs.text: This page defines naming conventions for the Enterprise AI Platform documentation and repository.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Ensure consistent naming across docs, filenames, and repository artifacts.
  • Help contributors find and update related documentation.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Use descriptive file names in lowercase with hyphens for docs.
  • Examples: architecture-overview.md, api-guidelines.md.
  • Use index.md for directory landing pages.

docs.title: Git and Branches
docs.text:
• Use meaningful branch names that describe the change.
  • Example: feature/docs-material-setup, fix/security-docs

docs.title: Code and Config
docs.text:
• Use PascalCase for C# types and records.
  • Use camelCase for JSON properties and configuration keys.
  • Use kebab-case for Markdown filenames and URL paths.

docs.title: Automated Documentation Generation
docs.text: This guide defines how the project generates and publishes documentation automatically.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Keep API documentation generated from the running application.
  • Keep architecture and operational docs version-controlled.
  • Provide a repeatable documentation generation process for CI.

docs.title: API Docs Automation
docs.text:
• Use native ASP.NET Core OpenAPI output for all runnable services.
  • Use Scalar as the interactive API documentation UI overlay.
  • Validate OpenAPI generation in CI as part of build and test gates.

docs.title: Docs Publishing
docs.text:
• Use Git-based documentation version control.
  • Publish docs alongside code changes via the repository.
  • Keep docs source files in docs/ and update them with feature or architecture changes.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
• Review the docs portal as part of each release.
  • Update the docs index and portal when new categories are added.

docs.title: CI/CD Quality Gates
docs.text: This document defines the CI/CD quality gates for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Gate Criteria
docs.text:
• dotnet restore and dotnet build must pass on every PR.
  • Unit tests must pass for touched projects.
  • Static analysis and linting should be enforced for code and documentation.
  • OpenAPI/Scalar API docs must generate successfully for runnable services.
  • Documentation updates must accompany code changes for public APIs and architecture decisions.

docs.title: Automation
docs.text:
• Use reusable pipeline steps to validate build, test, and documentation generation.
  • Fail fast on compilation errors, test failures, or missing documentation updates.
  • Enforce branch policies and PR reviews before merge.

docs.title: Audit and Traceability
docs.text:
• Keep CI run artifacts for failed builds and test results.
  • Link PRs to relevant ADRs, roadmap items, or release notes when applicable.

docs.text: This page defines Docker Compose practices for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:

docs.title: Docker
docs.text: This page defines Docker deployment practices for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Containerize services for consistency across development and deployment.
  • Enable reproducible builds and runtime environments.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Build Docker images from service project directories.
  • Use multistage Dockerfiles to separate build and runtime layers.
  • Keep images lean and avoid embedding secrets.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Use explicit base image versions.
  • Use health checks in container definitions.
  • Tag images with meaningful version or commit identifiers.

docs.title: Local Development
docs.text: This page defines local development deployment practices for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Provide a consistent local development environment.
  • Enable developers to build and run services locally with minimal friction.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Use the .NET 9 SDK defined in global.json.
  • Restore packages with dotnet restore.

docs.text:

  • Keep local secrets isolated from source control.

docs.title: Logging & Monitoring Guide
docs.text:
• Emit structured logs
  • Include correlation IDs on every request
  • Export traces and metrics via OpenTelemetry
  • Expose readiness and liveness endpoints

docs.title: Recommendations

docs.title: OpenTelemetry readiness
docs.text: The platform should use OpenTelemetry for tracing and metrics where possible, with logs enriched by correlation IDs and service context. This enables tracing of API requests, provider routing, policy decisions, and dependency health across distributed services.

docs.title: Correlation IDs
docs.text: This page defines correlation ID usage for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Track requests across services and logs.
  • Enable diagnostics of distributed requests.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Generate a correlation ID at API ingress.
  • Propagate the correlation ID through HTTP, messaging, and background work.
  • Include the correlation ID in logs, traces, and metric dimensions.
  • Respect any existing request ID header if provided by upstream load balancers or API gateways.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Use a stable header name such as X-Correlation-ID.
  • Emit the correlation ID in logs and trace context.
  • Avoid embedding sensitive data in the correlation ID.

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text: This page defines dashboard guidance for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Provide operational visibility for platform health and activity.
  • Expose trends for key platform metrics.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Create dashboards for request throughput, latency, error rate, and dependency health.
  • Include service-level and tenant-impact views where appropriate.
  • Surface alert conditions and capacity signals.
  • Keep dashboards focused, actionable, and easy to interpret.

docs.title: Recommended Widgets
docs.text:
• API request rate and success ratio
  • Error and exception counts
  • Average and P95/P99 latency
  • Provider adapter downstream latency and errors
  • Health check status summaries

docs.title: Health Checks
docs.text: This page defines health check expectations for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Verify service liveness and readiness.
  • Support container orchestrators and deployment health probes.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Expose a /health/live or /healthz endpoint for liveness.
  • Expose a /health/ready endpoint for readiness.
  • Include dependency health for databases, caches, provider credential stores, and configuration.
  • Keep liveness checks lightweight and suitable for restart behavior.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Return plain status for liveness and detailed dependency status for readiness.
  • Use OpenTelemetry health check integration where supported.
  • Document health endpoint contracts and expected HTTP status codes.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: This page defines logging practices for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Provide structured, searchable logs for platform operations and incidents.
  • Make logs useful for debugging and compliance.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Use structured JSON logs with consistent fields.
  • Include severity, timestamp, service name, tenant ID, and correlation ID.
  • Avoid logging secrets or sensitive payload content.
  • Capture error context and exception details.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry Integration
docs.text:
• Use OpenTelemetry-compatible log exporters when available.
  • Keep log schema consistent across services.
  • Use a central logging backend for indexing and searching logs.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: This page defines metrics practices for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Monitor service health and performance.
  • Drive alerts and capacity planning.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Emit request count, latency, error rate, and dependency metrics.
  • Use OpenTelemetry metrics conventions where applicable.
  • Tag metrics with service name, environment, and tenant context when relevant.
  • Use histogram or summary metrics for latency distribution.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Collect metrics at the service and host level.
  • Keep metric names consistent across services.
  • Use units and labels clearly in metric definitions.

docs.title: Observability Guide
docs.text: This guide defines observability expectations for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Ensure services emit consistent telemetry
  • Capture traces, metrics, and logs for key platform flows
  • Provide production visibility for API requests, authentication, and provider routing
  • Enable alerting on health, errors, and performance regressions

docs.title: Recommended Observability Pattern
docs.text:
• Distributed tracing for cross-service requests
  • Structured logs with correlation IDs
  • Metrics for request rates, error rates, latency, and dependency health
  • Health endpoints for liveness and readiness

docs.title: Key Observability Signals
docs.text:
• API request latency and success rate
  • Authentication and authorization failures
  • Provider adapter throughput and error trends
  • Policy decision latency and cache hit ratios
  • Database and cache dependency health

docs.title: Operational Use
docs.text:
• Use the logging and monitoring guide in deployment/logging-monitoring.md for deployment integration.
  • Ensure observability docs are updated when new telemetry or tracing requirements are added.

docs.title: Tracing
docs.text: This page defines tracing practices for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Visualize distributed requests across services.
  • Measure latency and identify bottlenecks.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Use OpenTelemetry tracing for cross-service requests.
  • Capture spans for API entry, routing, provider calls, and policy decisions.
  • Include service name, operation name, and status.
  • Propagate context through HTTP, gRPC, and background processing.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Record errors and exceptions on failed spans.
  • Use consistent span naming across services.
  • Link logs and traces using correlation IDs.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: Placeholder for operations runbooks, incident response, and support documentation.

docs.title: Operational Runbooks
docs.text: This runbook collection captures production operations guidance for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Runbook Scope
docs.text:
• service deployment checks
  • health probe behavior and remediation
  • service restarts and rollback guidance
  • capacity planning and scaling
  • database and cache failover procedures
  • incident response and escalation paths

docs.title: Health Check Operations
docs.text:
• Verify /health/live and /health/ready endpoints for every service.
  • Confirm the health check reflects dependencies such as Redis, PostgreSQL, and policy services.
  • Use container or orchestration probes to mark services healthy only when all critical dependencies are available.

docs.title: Service Restore
docs.text:
• Capture service logs and trace IDs before restart.
  • Restart the failing service from the platform host or container orchestrator.
  • Validate health endpoint and API readiness after restart.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Authentication failures: check JWT issuer, audiences, and token validation settings.
  • API docs issues: confirm OpenAPI generation and Scalar UI availability.
  • Configuration drift: compare deployed environment variables with documented values.

docs.title: Change Management
docs.text:
• Update this runbook when new service dependencies, host-level behaviors, or health probes are introduced.
  • Communicate operational changes in release notes and the project roadmap.

docs.title: Performance Guide
docs.text: This guide provides performance principles for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Performance Objectives
docs.text:
• Maintain low API latency for gateway and service endpoints
  • Keep prompt optimization overhead minimal
  • Ensure stateful stores and caches meet response SLAs
  • Optimize document ingestion and search performance for knowledge retrieval

docs.title: Performance Practices
docs.text:
• Use async, non-blocking I/O for all I/O-bound paths
  • Prefer caching for repeated prompt shapes and metadata lookups
  • Use batch and bulk operations for ingestion pipelines when appropriate
  • Apply rate limiting and throttling to protect shared services

docs.title: Measurement and Validation
docs.text:
• Capture performance metrics in production-like environments
  • Use load tests to validate service behavior under expected traffic
  • Monitor slow requests, dependency latency, and queue depth

docs.title: When to Update
docs.text: • Update this guide when service contracts change, new providers are added, or new scalability requirements emerge.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Placeholder for security guidance, authentication, and threat mitigation documentation.

docs.title: Audit Logging
docs.text: This page defines audit logging standards for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Capture security-relevant events for compliance and investigation.
  • Preserve tenant and request context for audit trails.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Log authentication and authorization decisions.
  • Record security-sensitive operations and configuration changes.
  • Include correlation identifiers and request context.
  • Avoid logging secrets and sensitive data.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Use structured logs for audit events.
  • Retain audit logs according to tenant and regulatory requirements.
  • Ensure logs are tamper-resistant and access-controlled.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: This page defines authentication standards for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Secure access to platform APIs and services.
  • Consistently validate client identity across boundaries.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Use JWT Bearer authentication for protected APIs.
  • Authenticate developers, service clients, and internal components.
  • Validate tokens centrally in each API layer.
  • Reject requests with missing, expired, or invalid tokens.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Use strong token signing keys and rotation policies.
  • Support audience and issuer validation.
  • Document authentication requirements in OpenAPI.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text: This page defines authorization standards for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Control access to tenant-scoped resources and operations.
  • Enforce role-based and policy-based permissions consistently.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Authorize every request after authentication.
  • Use role-based permissions for platform and tenant admin operations.
  • Use policy-based checks for resource and action-level decisions.
  • Deny by default for unknown or missing permissions.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Keep authorization logic separate from authentication.
  • Use tenant context for all authorization decisions.
  • Log denied access attempts for audit review.

docs.title: OWASP Guidelines
docs.text: This page summarizes OWASP security guidance relevant to the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Align platform security practices with industry standards.
  • Protect APIs and services against common web vulnerabilities.

docs.title: Key OWASP Principles
docs.text:
• Validate and sanitize all inputs.
  • Protect against injection attacks.
  • Use secure authentication and session management.
  • Enforce access control and avoid insecure direct object references.
  • Use secure defaults and minimize attack surface.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Validate payloads and request bodies.
  • Encode output and protect against cross-site attacks.
  • Secure API endpoints with authentication and authorization.
  • Log security events and errors without exposing sensitive data.

docs.title: Secrets Management
docs.text: This page defines secrets management practices for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Protect sensitive configuration and credentials.
  • Prevent secret exposure in source control or logs.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Keep secrets in a secure secret store.
  • Do not store secrets in repository files or configuration templates.
  • Use environment variables or secret references at runtime.
  • Rotate secrets regularly and revoke compromised credentials.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Encrypt secrets at rest and in transit.
  • Restrict access to secrets based on least privilege.
  • Avoid logging secrets or secret material.

docs.title: Secure Configuration
docs.text: This page defines secure configuration standards for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Ensure platform configuration is safe, manageable, and immutable where possible.
  • Prevent insecure defaults and configuration drift.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Use strong defaults for all runtime settings.
  • Require explicit opt-in for permissive or debug modes.
  • Keep configuration in environment-specific stores, not source control.
  • Validate configuration on startup.

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
• Use centralized configuration management for production.
  • Enforce least privilege and network restrictions via configuration.
  • Store sensitive values in secrets rather than plain text.

docs.title: Security Guide
docs.text:
• Require JWT Bearer auth for protected APIs
  • Treat tenant identity as a first-class input
  • Store secrets outside source control
  • Validate all incoming request data
  • Keep provider credentials in deployment secrets
  • Review API docs before exposing new endpoints publicly

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Placeholder for testing strategy, unit/integration tests, and quality validation documentation.

docs.title: API Testing
docs.text: This page defines API testing expectations for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Validate public and internal API contracts.
  • Confirm request/response schema, authentication, authorization, and error handling.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Use contract-driven tests against OpenAPI or generated API schemas.
  • Cover successful requests, validation failures, authentication errors, and authorization rules.
  • Validate API versioning and compatibility expectations.

docs.title: Bruno Collections
docs.text:
• Place Bruno collections in /api-tests.
  • Keep collections aligned with documented API contracts.
  • Use collections for regression coverage and automated endpoint validation.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Test the same response shapes that clients expect.
  • Include negative tests for invalid payloads and unauthorized access.
  • Document API test coverage in the docs portal.

docs.title: Integration Testing
docs.text: This page defines integration testing expectations for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Validate how platform components work together.
  • Confirm service contracts, middleware, persistence, and provider adapter behavior.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Use real service boundaries where practical, such as HTTP test servers and database fixtures.
  • Cover API middleware, authentication flows, routing, and data persistence.
  • Validate tenant isolation across service boundaries.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Use dedicated test resources for databases, Redis, and message connectors.
  • Keep tests repeatable by resetting state between runs.
  • Prefer lightweight integration tests for CI and reserve heavier end-to-end flows for targeted pipelines.
  • Use WebApplicationFactory, test fixtures, or containerized resources as appropriate.

docs.title: Performance Testing
docs.text: This page defines performance testing expectations for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Validate service scalability, latency, and throughput under load.
  • Identify performance regressions before production release.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Use realistic load profiles and service dependencies.
  • Measure request latency, error rate, and resource utilization.
  • Keep performance tests separate from functional CI runs.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Baseline critical API and provider adapter flows.
  • Use metrics and tracing to diagnose performance hotspots.
  • Record results and compare against historical performance targets.
  • Run load tests in an environment representative of production where feasible.

docs.title: Security Testing
docs.text: This page defines security testing expectations for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Validate that platform controls resist common security threats.
  • Confirm authentication, authorization, data protection, and input validation.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Include tests for authentication failure cases and token validation.
  • Validate authorization boundaries for tenant isolation and service-level access.
  • Test input validation, injection resistance, and secure error handling.
  • Confirm secrets are not exposed in logs or error responses.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Use automated security test suites alongside functional tests.
  • Add regression coverage for discovered vulnerabilities.
  • Document known security test scenarios in the docs.

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text: This document defines the testing strategy for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Testing Levels
docs.text:
• Unit tests for domain, application, and shared building block behavior
  • Integration tests for service contracts, API middleware, and persistence interactions
  • End-to-end tests for gateway workflows, authentication, and provider routing
  • Regression tests for documentation, schema, and tooling behavior

docs.title: Quality Goals
docs.text:
• Validate tenant isolation and policy enforcement in tests
  • Keep tests fast and deterministic where possible
  • Measure coverage for application and shared kernel logic
  • Validate critical API routes with contract tests

docs.title: Recommended Practices
docs.text:
• Use xUnit for unit and integration testing in .NET projects
  • Use dedicated test fixtures for database and Redis-backed tests
  • Keep API tests aligned with OpenAPI documentation and endpoint schemas
  • Add tests when introducing behavior changes or architectural primitives

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Document test patterns in this file so new contributors understand the testing expectations.
  • Link test strategy guidance from CONTRIBUTING.md and the docs portal.

docs.title: Unit Testing
docs.text: This page defines unit testing expectations for the Enterprise AI Platform.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Validate logic in isolation.
  • Prove domain invariants, application services, and utility helpers.
  • Keep tests fast, deterministic, and easy to maintain.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
• Use xUnit for .NET unit tests.
  • Test one behavior per test method.
  • Use clear naming conventions such as MethodName_StateUnderTest_ExpectedResult.
  • Prefer mocks or fakes for external dependencies.
  • Test validation rules, business logic, and small transformation functions.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep unit tests isolated from databases, caches, external APIs, and file systems.
  • Use test fixtures only where shared in-memory setup reduces duplication.
  • Add tenant-aware assertions in tests involving tenant-specific behavior.
  • Focus on behavior over implementation details.
